decisionMemo.businessProblem: A collaboration SaaS growing 45% is seeing its expansion engine seize because users stop using the product. In-account active adoption (weekly active / licensed seats) fell from 62% to 38% over 18 months while feature count tripled; NRR fell 118%→104% as seat expansion stalled; support tickets per seat rose 55% with 'too complicated' (34%) and 'can't find feature' (28%) as top themes. Power users (top 15%) stay highly engaged, but the broad licensed base disengages, and new seats reach active use only 29% of the time within 60 days. The owner suspects simplicity and expansion problems and weighs both a simplification effort and new expansion features (the cultural default of shipping). The real pattern is a usability/trust failure inside accounts: feature bloat buries core workflows (median clicks-to-core-task up 40%; 11 of 60+ features drive 80% of usage), so non-power users abandon the product, trust in daily use erodes, and seat expansion becomes impossible. With Series C gated on NRR/seat expansion and 28 months of runway, the owner must decide whether to keep shipping features or fix the in-account adoption/trust failure.
